audit.whatIsWrong: diff reads FAV while the tone token is the red 'hard' colour.
audit.why: 55.63% over 1839 games. The lane is genuinely miserable for five levels and then decided by Mundo's scaling — FAV with the orange token is the honest read; red says 'you lose this' at a glance.
audit.corrected: tone recoloured to the FAV token. Difficulty left at 8/10, which the mirror also endorsed.

audit.whatIsWrong: win[4..6] and phases[4..6].side read 'Skill' for Level 6, First item and 2+ items — the three stages this matchup is actually decided by. The content prose also disagreed with itself: whys[2] and whys[3] claim the lane flips to you at level 3, while whys[4] says 'at 6 he re-spikes' and spikes[1] says your R flips every all-in at 6.
audit.why: The mirror (jayce__drmundo, point 2) states the agreed shape: Jayce owns levels 1 through 5 because Mundo has no answer to accelerated Shock Blast, and the lane turns at 6 and again at first item. Both directions must say the same thing.
audit.corrected: Level 6, First item and 2+ items flipped to Dr. Mundo as one atomic group (2+ items rating 5/10 -> 7/10), and whys[2], whys[3], whys[4], phases[2].why, phases[3].why, spikes[0].text, early and mid rewritten so levels 3 to 5 read as Jayce's and the flip lands at 6 where the mirror puts it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Shock Blast was given a flat 6s cooldown and described only as 'his main poke'. Two interactions were missing: Acceleration Gate is cast FIRST and increases the missile's speed, range and damage when Shock Blast is fired through it — that is the tell and it dictates which way you sidestep — and Jayce's weapon swap is a 6s auto-attack reset whose first attack in Cannon form reduces both your Armor and Magic Resist.
audit.why: The armour/MR shred is why 'just build resists' does not solve this lane, and 'step across the gate, not along it' is the concrete dodging rule the page never gave.
audit.corrected: Real cooldown (16s at rank 1, 6s maxed), gate-then-blast sequencing and the sidestep direction written into breakdown.cooldowns, report[5], phases[2].why and spikes[0].text.

audit.why: 16/14/12/10/8/6 — 6s is only the fully-ranked value, and at rank 1 the 16s downtime is a real window the page was hiding.

edits.before: Level 3 Q Infected Bonesaw lets you bar-clear and out-sustain his draining mana pool.
edits.after: Level 3 stays his: Shock Blast through Acceleration Gate outranges your bonesaw.

edits.before: Through levels 4-5 your health regen and W Heart Zapper beat his fading poke pressure.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay his: accelerated Shock Blast chips faster than your regen returns.

edits.before: At 6 he re-spikes: his hammer knockback plus empowered all-in can burst you before R value.
edits.after: At 6 you flip it: R Maximum Dosage heals a share of your missing health, 120s flat.

edits.before: Full kit online and your passive shrugs the first CC. Cleaver poke plus E-empowered swats start the grind; never brawl while Shock Blast is up.
edits.after: Full kit online, but Shock Blast is 16s at rank 1 and hits harder through his Gate. Farm at range and step up only inside that long downtime.

edits.before: Q ranks make the cleaver chunk real HP and your passive regen ramps. Jayce must kill you through the sustain or watch you out-scale — most can't.
edits.after: Q ranks and your regen both ramp, but accelerated Shock Blast still chips faster. Hold the wave near your tower and wait for Maximum Dosage at 6.

edits.before: Once you hit 3 you can bar-clear with Q Infected Bonesaw and walk through his Q-E poke; his mana runs dry long before your health bar does, so you start winning the sustained trade even though he wins the burst.
edits.after: Levels 3-5 still belong to him: Shock Blast fired through Acceleration Gate gains range, missile speed and damage, and the gate is always cast first — sidestep across it, never along it, and farm at max range until 6.

edits.before: Jayce owns levels 1-2: his ranged Q Shock Blast through Acceleration Gate outranges everything you have and chunks you before you get Q online, so hug the wave and just farm — do not walk up to trade a hammer melee you can't reach.
edits.after: Jayce owns levels 1-5: his ranged Q Shock Blast through Acceleration Gate outranges everything you have and chips faster than you regenerate, so hug the wave and just farm — do not walk up to trade a hammer melee you can't reach.

edits.before: By level 3 you flip it — Q Infected Bonesaw sustains you back up while his mana drains, and once you hit R Maximum Dosage at 6 his all-in combo (knockback + empowered melee) just heals off you and you out-DPS him with W and E.
edits.after: Level 6 is where you flip it — R Maximum Dosage instantly heals a share of your missing health on a flat 120s, so his all-in combo (knockback into empowered melee) heals off you and you out-DPS him with W and E ticking.

edits.before: - Jayce Shock Blast (6s): matchup-defining — His main poke. Dodge it. Track it before every commit. - Your ultimate: spend it on kill windows, never on waves. - Summoners: track his Flash after any close call — it changes every dive call.
edits.after: - Jayce Shock Blast (16s at rank 1, 6s maxed): his main poke — the Acceleration Gate lands first, so sidestep across the gate, never along it. - Your ultimate: spend it on kill windows, never on waves. - Summoners: track his Flash after a close call.

edits.before: Track Jayce’s Shock Blast (6s): His main poke. Dodge it. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Shock Blast is 16s at rank 1; through Acceleration Gate it gains range, speed and damage — step across the gate.

edits.before: His windows: Level 1, Level 2, Level 3, Levels 4-5. Fight at your spikes, concede his — the level chart above is the trade calendar.
edits.after: His windows: Level 1 to Levels 4-5. Yours: Level 6 on. Fight at your spikes, concede his — the level chart above is the trade calendar.

edits.before: See the level-by-level chart — fight in your windows (your item spikes), respect his (Level 1, Level 2, Level 3, Levels 4-5).
edits.after: See the level-by-level chart — fight in your windows (Level 6 and both item stages), respect his (Level 1 to Levels 4-5).

notes: Aligned to the mirror rather than to the packet levelChart: the packet gives Mundo levels 3 and 4-5 and hands Jayce level 6, which is the opposite of what jayce__drmundo settled on ('Jayce owns levels 1 through 5, the lane turns at 6 and again at first item'). I followed the mirror. Jayce's first Cannon-form attack reduces BOTH Armor and Magic Resist on a 6s swap — that is why flat resists do not answer this lane; it has no natural home inside any existing field's length band and deserves a dedicated one. tradeGood and breakdown.trading carry scraped PDF junk ('• • Dr. Mundo Top Lane Matchup Database 64').
